result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.directed_cycle_basis()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a fundamental cycle basis for a directed graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16686-L16756){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.directed_cycle_basis() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Directed cycle basis](/assets/graphs/directed-cycle-basis.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The house-shaped graph with directed edges, one strongly connected component. With 6 edges and 5 nodes the basis has 6 − 5 + 1 = 2 cycles, each following the arrows: the triangle A, B, C in the accent color and the outer loop A, B, D, E, C in teal, each listed from its lowest node." width="100%"} For a directed graph, the cycle space operates over the rationals (not GF(2) as in the undirected case). A fundamental cycle basis is computed by finding the strongly connected components (SCCs), building a DFS arborescence in each non-trivial SCC, and extracting one directed cycle per non-tree edge. The number of cycles returned equals `m - n + p` where `m` is the number of edges, `n` the number of nodes, and `p` the number of strongly connected components (counting isolated nodes and acyclic components). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of directed cycles forming the cycle basis. Each cycle is a list of node IDs `[v0, v1, ..., vk]` representing the closed walk `v0 -> v1 -> ... -> vk -> v0`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If called on an undirected graph (use `cycle_basis()` instead). ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Unlike the undirected cycle basis (which operates over GF(2) with symmetric differences), the directed cycle space uses signed incidence vectors over the rationals: each arc traversed forward gets +1, backward -1, and unused arcs get 0. The dimension of the directed cycle space is $m - n + p$ where $p$ is the number of strongly connected components, and this function returns exactly that many cycles. The algorithm runs in $O(V + E)$ time per SCC, so overall $O(V + E)$ for the entire graph. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A simple directed triangle has a single fundamental cycle: ::: {#8f2c103c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) ) cycles = graph.directed_cycle_basis() len(cycles) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: A figure-eight has two fundamental cycles: ::: {#48524efc .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("A", "D"), ("D", "A")]) ) cycles = graph.directed_cycle_basis() len(cycles) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: :::
